research_question: Can we establish a task-aligned, reproducible clone-discovery reference evaluation before assessing Rust-specific extensions?

selected_reference.name: BigCloneBench V2 via BigCloneEval
selected_reference.reason: Known clone discovery and range-based recall are aligned with the existing SourcererCC baseline, unlike query retrieval or library generation

actual_acquisition.response: HTTP 200 HTML landing pages; no gzip archive magic in bounded prefixes

entry_gates: Obtain exact V2 database and corresponding reduced source corpus; archive version, size, digest and source links
Separate benchmark database license from per-file corpus licenses; no automatic raw-data redistribution
Record database schema and eligible reference denominators before running a detector
Check reference source coordinates and detector range projection using boundary fixtures
Verify chosen coverage matcher mode by executing controlled integration tests before benchmark scoring
Freeze functionality/source slice selection independently of detector outputs; both endpoints of every evaluated pair must lie within scanned input
Report subset protocol as subset evaluation, not whole benchmark recall or original paper reproduction
resource_policy: Current work limited to pinned metadata and bounded share entry probes; no full VM, paid service, login or speculative mirrors. A later bulk transfer requires size and integrity plan, not a repeated blind crawl.
next_actions: Resolve the official public file-download route or another author-confirmed release; if it requires credentials, retain gap and do not bypass access controls
Execute a small evaluator/range-mapping integration test separately from any dataset score
Prepare a separately identified Rust mechanism-suite protocol with constructive relations and independent checking, without treating seen xkernel examples as held-out
